name: MakiRoll
subcategory: talking head video recording and editing
tagline: iOS app for shooting and cleaning up talking head videos: teleprompter, captions, trimming, vertical export.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The pieces of a talking head pipeline are all commodity now: ffmpeg for cutting and cropping, a local Whisper model for transcription and caption burn-in, simple energy detection for dead air and filler words. An agent can wire that into a local tool in a weekend and the output will be genuinely close on the editing side. What it will not produce is an iPhone app you open at a traffic light: the camera capture, the teleprompter that scrolls at the right speed over a live preview, the stabilization, the share sheet, the thing surviving a phone call mid-record. If you shoot on your phone and edit at a desk, the DIY version is fine. If the whole point is that recording and publishing happen on the same device in four minutes, you are rebuilding a mobile app, which is not a one-shot.
coreLoopDIY: Takes a raw self-shot video, transcribes it locally, cuts silences and filler words, burns styled captions, and exports a vertical crop ready to post.
requirements: Python 3.11 and a few GB of disk for a local Whisper model
A machine that can transcribe without melting, Apple Silicon or any GPU helps
You still shoot the footage on your phone and move files around
whatYouLose: Recording on the phone itself, with a teleprompter over the live camera preview
One-tap export to the share sheet and straight into TikTok or Reels
Caption styling presets that already look like what people expect, instead of whatever your first pass at ASS subtitles looks like
Auto framing and face tracking during capture, which you cannot fake in post
Someone else maintaining the thing when a codec or an OS update breaks it
moatNotes: The defensible part is the capture experience on a specific device, not the edit list. Post-production is ffmpeg with opinions.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the editing is the easy half. Paying for this buys a capture loop that works on the device where the footage is already sitting, and a set of caption and crop defaults that look right the first time. A local pipeline gets you equivalent output with an extra step of airdropping files to a laptop and waiting for transcription, which is exactly the kind of friction that stops people from posting at all.
notes: The edit pipeline is a weekend; the phone is the product.
prompt:
Build a local command line tool called "makicut" that turns a raw talking head recording into a post-ready vertical video.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Python 3.11, uv for dependency management, Typer for the CLI.
- faster-whisper for local transcription, model size configurable, default "small".
- ffmpeg and ffprobe invoked as subprocesses. Assume they are on PATH and fail loudly with a clear message if not.
- No cloud APIs, no accounts, no telemetry, no network calls at runtime except the one-time Whisper model download.

Commands:
1. `makicut transcribe INPUT` : writes a word-level JSON transcript next to the input.
2. `makicut plan INPUT` : from the transcript plus audio loudness, emits a cut plan JSON listing segments to keep. Drop silences longer than a configurable threshold, default 600ms, and drop words matching a filler list in config.toml, default um, uh, like, you know, so, basically. Keep 120ms of padding on each side of a keep segment.
3. `makicut render INPUT` : applies the cut plan with ffmpeg concat, crops to 1080x1920 centered on a fixed crop box, burns captions as ASS subtitles, writes OUTPUT.mp4.
4. `makicut run INPUT` : all three in order.

Captions: generate an ASS file from the word timings, two to four words per line, bold sans-serif, white text with a thick black outline, bottom third, one line highlighted word by word. Put the font, size, colors and vertical offset in config.toml.

Editing the plan: `plan` also writes a plain-text transcript where each line is a keep segment. If the user deletes lines from that file and reruns `render`, honor the edits. That is the only review UI. Do not build a GUI.

Explicitly out of scope: camera capture, teleprompter, face tracking, background removal, music, uploading anywhere.

Deliverables: working CLI, config.toml with sane defaults, a README showing a full run on a sample file, and a .env.example only if you end up needing any secret at all (you should not). Make `makicut run sample.mp4` work end to end before you call it done.
